rows.description: A toddler bangs a spoon, claps or refuses a food because the child beside them does. This is pure imitation with no idea of rules or approval, yet it is the root of later fitting in.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child insists on the same bottle colour, the same game rules and the same dance step as the group. Sameness feels safe and being different feels like being left out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Changing an answer after others answer [Actor]
rows.description: A child who knew the right answer changes it when most of the class says otherwise. Doubting oneself feels easier than being the lone voice, even when privately certain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Sudden shifts in taste and friends [Observer]
rows.description: A parent notices new slang, music and a new friend circle. Curiosity and steady interest work better than ridicule, which pushes the teen further into the group.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler stops or goes on according to the caregiver's face and tone. They obey the emotional signal more than the words, which is how authority is first felt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child obeys quickly when an adult's voice turns sharp, to avoid disapproval. The behaviour looks like good discipline while the inner state is anxiety.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child is told by an older student or adult to hide something, pick on someone or keep a secret. They feel a pull between obedience and a stomach-sinking sense of wrongness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A new intern or ragging-era junior does what a senior demands to avoid punishment or gain favour. Responsibility feels moved to the person giving the order, which is exactly how harm gets done.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A colleague sees a peer quietly doing something dubious on instruction. Asking a plain question, is this okay, gives the person space to pause without being accused.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A group of teens planning an event rushes to agree with the loudest member. Nobody wants to spoil the mood, so doubts stay unspoken and a poor plan goes ahead.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
